items.followUp: Describe Rutherford’s experiment that led to the discovery of the proton.

rubric.why: Identifies the experiment used to produce the penetrating radiation.
rubric.description: Chadwick bombarded beryllium with alpha particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming beryllium and alpha particles, or helium nuclei.

rubric.why: Shows how the radiation led to the identification of the neutron.
rubric.description: The radiation knocked protons out of paraffin wax; because it was neutral, Chadwick identified it as neutrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the protons knocked out of paraffin wax or identifying the radiation as neutral neutrons.

modelAnswer: Chadwick bombarded beryllium with alpha particles; a highly penetrating radiation was produced.
When this radiation struck paraffin wax, it knocked out protons; being uncharged and having a mass nearly equal to a proton, it was identified as neutrons.

items.followUp: Explain why atomic radius decreases from left to right across a period.

rubric.why: Identifies the increase in nuclear charge across a period as the cause of the trend.
rubric.description: Ionization energy increases from left to right across a period because nuclear charge increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the direction of the trend and linking it to increasing nuclear charge.

rubric.why: Explains that increased distance or shielding weakens the attraction to the outer electron down a group.
rubric.description: Ionization energy decreases down a group because atomic radius and shielding increase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the downward trend and linking it to increased shielding or greater distance from the nucleus.

modelAnswer: Across a period, nuclear charge increases while atomic radius decreases, so the outer electron is attracted more strongly and more energy is needed to remove it.
Down a group, atomic radius and shielding increase, so the outer electron is less strongly attracted and less energy is needed to remove it.
